assessments.technical_explanation: The scanner flagged 19 unsafe-regex occurrences. The visible patterns are complex regular expressions used for parsing roleplay chat text, speaker cues, CSS snippets, and HTML scaffolding. Many use bounded lazy quantifiers such as [\s\S]{0,1400}? which limits but does not fully eliminate catastrophic backtracking risk on adversarial input. The input domain is the user's own chat session content in a local roleplay client. The worst concrete outcome would be a frozen tab or slowdown when processing a specifically crafted message—a local self-denial-of-service with low impact and no cross-user or system harm.
assessments.layman_explanation: The plugin uses many complex text-matching rules to parse chat messages. Some of these rules could theoretically slow down the browser if fed specially crafted text, but only on the user's own machine with their own chat content. The worst case is a temporary slowdown or frozen tab, not data loss or security breach.
assessments.developer_action: Consider testing the most complex regex patterns against pathological inputs and adding input-length guards or simplifying patterns that show significant backtracking.

These operate on user-authored prompt text within a local plugin context. A crafted input could potentially cause a frozen tab, but the impact is a recoverable local denial of service with no data loss, credential exposure, or cross-user harm. Per the threat model, this is low impact.
assessments.layman_explanation: Some text-parsing patterns in the code could be slow if given very unusual input, potentially freezing the browser tab. This is a minor code quality issue with no risk of data loss or security breach, and only affects the user's own session.
assessments.developer_action: Consider reviewing tagged-prompt regexes for catastrophic backtracking on adversarial input; anchor and simplify alternations where feasible to prevent tab freezes.

assessments.technical_explanation: The JS-X-Ray shady-link signal flagged fixed URL literals in the vendored UI bundle. The visible source contains two distinct destinations: a localhost backend at 127.0.0.1:28120 (the plugin's own local backend service) and the official NovelAI image generation API endpoint at image.novelai.net. Both destinations are proportionate to the project's stated purpose of generating images through NovelAI or ComfyUI and communicating with its local backend. No third-party, obfuscated, or unexpected external endpoints are present in the supplied evidence. The scanner did not retain matched values, and no exfiltration data flow is visible.
assessments.layman_explanation: The flagged links are the plugin's own local backend address and the official NovelAI image API — exactly what this image-generating plugin is supposed to talk to. Nothing suspicious was found.

assessments.technical_explanation: The scanner evidence is confined to a proven non-runtime scope and does not demonstrate user harm.
assessments.layman_explanation: This technical signal is not part of the shipped runtime behavior.

observations.title: Sensitive data is redacted before persistence and serialization
observations.technical_explanation: Multiple functions strip data-URI image payloads and exclude internal debug fields before writing to storage or returning API responses. An API key test function checks presence without logging the key value. These patterns are consistent with intentional data hygiene rather than credential exposure.
observations.layman_explanation: The plugin actively removes sensitive image data and avoids exposing API key values when saving or returning data, which is a positive security practice.

observations.title: CDN image access tokens in guide HTML are not credentials
observations.technical_explanation: All six candidates are the same pattern: key query parameters on image URLs from a public CDN, each paired with an expires timestamp. They appear only in a static HTML guide file and grant time-limited read access to screenshots. No executable code, credential store, model-provider key, or sensitive data flow is involved.
observations.layman_explanation: Every flagged item is just a temporary link key for showing screenshots in the help page. They are not passwords or API keys and cannot be used to access anything sensitive.
